note: The warning fires whenever an update leaves the incident resolved or closed, using the status the API returns. That is the owner's decision (fire whenever the update leaves the incident resolved), and it also covers updates that do not pass --status. Updating an already resolved incident that still has open events is a case the warning is meant to surface.

On a mid-pagination failure the warning lists only the open events it did see, which is still accurate and useful. The check is best-effort by decision: a failed lookup is reported as a debug note at most, so the command output stays quiet and unchanged. Counting from earlier pages is not worth a new 'incomplete' wording.

One shared deadline across the alert fetch, all pages and all related incidents is a deliberate trade-off, and was requested in review so the optional check can never delay the command by more than 10 seconds in total. Per-incident timeouts would multiply that bound. A late timeout is silent by the same best-effort decision.
